title: No one owns anything forever
takeaway: Looks, youth and power are all on loan. Don't be proud of them.
scene: This ghazal is printed in two columns. Each row is one couplet. The poet looks at the world and sees that nothing in it lasts.

original: ننگے پیر تے جسیاں اتے لیر نئیں
ہجر تیرے وچ کیہڑا جو دلگیر نئیں
transliteration: Nange pair te jussiyaan utte leer nahin
Hijr tere vich kehra jo dilgeer nahin
translation: Bare feet, and not a rag on their bodies:
who isn't heartbroken from being apart from You?
couplets.story: He sees people walking barefoot in rags, who have lost everything. He asks: is there anyone who isn't heartbroken, being so far from the Beloved?

original: پیار ظلم تے نیکی دھوکا اوڑک دا
کسے وی شے دی ایتھے کوئی آخیر نئیں
transliteration: Pyaar zulm te neki dhokha orak da
Kise vi shai di ethe koi aakheer nahin
translation: In the end, love turns to cruelty and kindness to betrayal.
Nothing here lasts to the end.
couplets.story: In this world, even good things go bad. Love can turn cruel and kindness can turn into a trick. Nothing here is permanent.

original: مان نہ کریئے جوبن روپ، جوانی دا
سدا کسے دی سجناں ایہہ جاگیر نئیں
transliteration: Maan na kariye joban roop, jawaani da
Sada kise di sajnaan eh jaageer nahin
translation: Don't be proud of your bloom, your looks, your youth:
my friend, these are no one's property forever.
couplets.story: Don't get proud of being young and good-looking. You don't own those things. They're borrowed, and everybody has to give them back one day.

original: روے تیرے رنگ اڈایا پھلاں دا
سورج چن ستاریاں وچ تنویر نئیں
transliteration: Roop tere rang udaaya phullaan da
Sooraj chann sitaariyaan vich tanveer nahin
translation: Your face has drained the colour from the flowers;
the sun, moon and stars have no light left beside it.
couplets.story: Next to the Beloved's face, flowers look pale. The sun, the moon and the stars look dim.

original: ایہہ تسبیح ہے دانے ورد پکاندے نیں
اکھاں دیوچ انج تے سجنا نیر نئیں
transliteration: Eh tasbeeh hai daane, vird pakaande nain
Akhaan de vich inj te sajna neer nahin
translation: These are prayer beads; each bead repeats its prayer.
My love, these aren't just tears in my eyes.
couplets.story: His tears fall one after another, like the beads on a string of prayer beads. Each tear is like a prayer being counted. They're not just tears.

original: ہر اک گھٹیا وٹیا سہمیاں پھردا اے
ہاسے ونڈن والی کوئی تصویر نئیں
transliteration: Har ik ghuttiya vattiya sehmiyaan phirda ae
Haase vandan vaali koi tasveer nahin
translation: Everyone goes about tense and frightened;
there isn't a single face handing out smiles.
couplets.story: Everyone walks around stressed and scared. He can't find a single face that's sharing a smile.

original: جھاتی مار پچھانو واسی شہر دیو
راہوں کھنجیا میں کوئی راہ گیر نئیں
transliteration: Jhaati maar pachhaano vaasi shehar deo
Raahon khunjiya main koi raahgeer nahin
translation: People of this city, take a good look and recognise me:
I'm no passing stranger who's lost his way.
couplets.story: He calls out to the people of his town. Look at me properly. I'm not some stranger who got lost. I belong here.

original: اکھ چرائی ساڈے توں مونہہ موڑ لیا
سانوں سجناں دسی کوئی تقصیر نئیں
transliteration: Akh churaai saade ton moonh mor liya
Saanu sajnaan dassi koi taqseer nahin
translation: You avoided my eyes and turned your face away,
without telling me, my love, what I did wrong.
couplets.story: The beloved stopped looking at him and turned away, and never told him what he did wrong.

original: نال محبت سینے تینوں لاوے کون؟
احمدؔ تیریاں ہاواں وچ تاثیر نئیں
transliteration: Naal mohabbat seene tainu laave kaun?
Ahmad teriyaan haavaan vich taaseer nahin
translation: Who's going to hold you to their heart with love?
Ahmad, your sighs have no power to move anyone.
couplets.story: He ends by teasing himself. Who's going to hug you, Ahmad? Your sighs aren't moving anyone.

deeper: 'Nothing here lasts' and 'youth is no one's property forever' echo the Qur'an's reminder that everything on earth passes away and only God remains (55:26–27). The tears falling like prayer beads (tasbeeh) is a striking Sufi image: grief itself becomes a kind of worship, each tear a remembrance of God.
why: It's a reminder that is easy to forget at any age: what you look like and what you own are temporary.
prompt: What's something you're proud of that you know won't last? What would still matter without it?
notes: Printed in two columns; each row is read as one couplet (right line first).
